title: Day 57 · Week 8, Day 1 — Brain: the factory opens — a hundred and seventy thousand neurons a minute from yesterday to Day 122, the first reflex ever filmed, and the dose of a chest X-ray against the line the bombs drew
summary: The fifth Brain episode. Your baby is at Carnegie stage 18 (13–17 mm; the NHS raspberry), the femur's shaft turning to bone today by the Keibel & Mall timetable, the hemispheres hollow bubbles whose walls are almost entirely factory. The schedule from Stiles & Jernigan 2010: neural progenitors in the ventricular zone divide symmetrically from embryonic day 25 to 42 (Day 39–56), doubling the pool; from E42 — yesterday — division turns asymmetric and each round yields a neuron that will never divide again; neocortical neurogenesis is essentially complete by about E108 (Day 122). The arithmetic: ~16 billion cortical neurons (Azevedo 2009) in 66 days is about 170,000 a minute, against Cowan's whole-brain 250,000. The preplate, its splitting into marginal zone and subplate, the cortical plate from stage 21 (~Day 63), inside-out layering, and the finding that the radial glia guiding migration are the progenitors themselves — Rakic's radial unit made of cells. The first reflex: Hooker 1936 (Yale J Biol Med), a 25 mm fetus turning neck and trunk away from a hair drawn across the mouth, a spinal circuit a week or so from now, with his own caveats; why it differs from the spontaneous bends of Day 49, and why neither is a feeling. Then the one physical thing that can reach a tissue of dividing cells: ionising radiation. Otake & Schull's atomic-bomb reanalysis (1996): severe intellectual disability concentrated at 8–15 weeks after ovulation — Day 70 to Day 119, matching the factory's run; CDC/NCRP 174: 40% with IQ <70 after 1 Gy at 8–15 weeks, 15% at 16–25, non-cancer effects not detectable below 100 mGy; ACOG Committee Opinion 723: nothing associated with anomalies or loss below 50 mGy, intellectual disability only documented at ≥610 mGy. The doses: chest X-ray 0.0005–0.01 mGy, extremity <0.001, head CT 0.001–0.01, chest CT/CTPA 0.01–0.66, abdominal X-ray 0.1–3, lumbar spine 1–10, abdominal CT 1.3–35, pelvic CT 10–50 (≈2.5 low-dose), technetium scans <5; ten thousand chest films to the 100 mGy line; background ~1 mSv a year; a flight under 0.1 mSv (Day 32). The cancer side, which has no threshold: the Oxford Survey's leukaemia RR 1.49 (1.33–1.67) after ~6 mGy obstetric films; Wakeford & Little's 8% per Gy excess absolute childhood cancer risk on a baseline of ~1 in 630 — about 1 in 500 extra from a 25 mGy abdominal CT, about 1 in a million from a chest film. ACOG's rule: a needed scan is a needed scan; ultrasound and MRI first for the abdomen and pelvis; dental films safe (ACOG CO 569). And lead: Hu 2006 (146 Mexico City pairs; first-trimester lead predicted 24-month MDI, −3.5 points per SD plasma lead, later trimesters did not), the CDC 2010 risk-factor list for the first visit, the 5 µg/dL line, bone lead mobilised in pregnancy, and the sanding rule.
action: Ten minutes tonight, two lines in the pregnancy file. One: on the Day 40 question sheet, question fourteen in two parts — any X-rays or scans she has had since Day 14 (what and roughly when), and the lead risk list read out loud together (house age and any sanding, her work, imported food and glazed pottery, remedies and cosmetics, hobbies); if any item is a yes, write 'blood lead test?' beside it. Two: a card behind her insurance card that says 'I'm pregnant' with the due date, for whoever holds the X-ray button. If any renovation is planned before Day 280, write the rule on page one: she is out of the building for sanding or scraping, dust is contained and wet-wiped, and paint in a house older than 1978 is tested before it is touched.
